exercises.prompt: With which hadith does Sahih al-Bukhari open?
exercises.explanation: The very first hadith of the most authentic collection is about intention - because the heart decides the value of everything.

source.text: Actions are only judged by intentions, and every person will have what he intended.

exercises.prompt: Two people give the same $100 to charity; one for Allah and one for a photo-op. What differs?
exercises.explanation: The Quran warns that what follows a charity can void it: showing off burns the very deed that looked good.

source.text: O you who believe, do not invalidate your charities with reminders of it or injury, like one who spends to be seen by people.

options.text: The photo adds reach, so more reward
The same action earns reward or nothing depending on the heart behind it

exercises.prompt: What is riya?
exercises.explanation: The Quran calls it out sharply: woe to those who pray to be seen - worship with an audience in mind.

source.text: So woe to those who pray, yet are heedless of their prayer, those who make a show of their deeds.

options.text: Doing good deeds so people see and praise you
Reciting the Quran aloud in prayer
Giving charity where it is most needed

exercises.prompt: Can a deed done for people’s praise carry reward?
exercises.explanation: The Quran’s condition: righteous work plus no partner associated in the worship - the motive is part of the act.

source.text: So whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous work and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.

options.text: No - Allah accepts only what is done purely for Him alone
Yes, if the deed itself is good

exercises.prompt: Why is secret charity described as a protection?
exercises.explanation: The closer a deed is to secrecy, the further it is from riya - some scholars kept their best deeds hidden from everyone.

source.text: A man who gives in charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends is among those shaded on the Day of Judgement.

options.text: It guarantees the money is used well
It hides the deed from the desire for praise - only Allah sees it
It is embarrassing to give publicly

exercises.prompt: What single question helps separate riya from sincerity?
exercises.explanation: The heart-check question: deeds that survive zero visibility are deeds built for Allah.

source.text: Whoever makes his good deeds heard of for show, Allah will expose his reality.

options.text: "Would I still do this if no human could ever find out?"

exercises.prompt: You film your street charity delivery for content. What remains of the reward?
exercises.explanation: The deed is judged by the intention behind it; a camera changes the motive test, not the number of meals delivered.

source.text: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders of it or injury, like one who spends to be seen by people.

options.text: Whatever was genuinely for Allah; the showing-off part earns no reward

exercises.prompt: A man prays beautifully when the group watches but rushes alone. What describes him?
exercises.explanation: The tell is the shift: worship should look the same whether one human or zero humans can see.

source.text: Those who make a show of their deeds.

options.text: A person with a quiet style
A person whose worship shifts with the audience - riya has entered

exercises.prompt: The scholar of that hadith learned and taught. Where did he go wrong?
exercises.explanation: The third man of the hadith: knowledge used as currency for reputation turns the same lessons into evidence against the teacher.

source.text: He learned knowledge and taught it and recited Quran to be called a scholar and a reciter. It was said: you have received what you wanted.

options.text: He sought to be called a scholar for himself
He taught only a few people

exercises.prompt: The martyr of that hadith fought bravely and died - what was his verdict?
exercises.explanation: Even bravery on the battlefield is weighed by motive - the most dramatic deed can be hollowed out by an audience of one’s own reputation.

source.text: He fought to be called brave. It was said: you have received what you wanted.

options.text: He fought so it would be said he was brave; he is dragged into the Fire
He was forgiven for his courage

exercises.prompt: In the famous hadith of the three men judged first, why is the generous man condemned despite his charity?
exercises.explanation: Muslim 1905 tells of three people whose impressive deeds were exposed by their motives - the wealthy man wanted the label, and got it.

source.text: A man whom Allah gave wealth: he spent for show. It was said to him: you have received what you wanted.

options.text: He gave to be called generous - and received that title instead of reward
He gave to the wrong people

exercises.prompt: What single thread unites all three men of Muslim 1905?
exercises.explanation: Three different arenas - wealth, war, scholarship - and one shared defect: visibility mattered more than Allah’s acceptance.

source.text: All three were brought and judged first, and all three were told: you have received what you wanted.

options.text: They acted for people’s praise instead of for Allah
They all lacked sincerity in worship only
They broke the law in secret

exercises.prompt: What are practical daily shields against riya?
exercises.explanation: The habit pattern: intentions refreshed at the start of acts, and a private reserve of deeds with zero witnesses.

source.text: Whoever intends show, Allah will expose; the one who keeps some deeds private protects their sincerity.

options.text: Renewing intention often and hiding some good deeds completely
Announcing your charity so it spreads

exercises.prompt: What dua is taught as the shield against hidden shirk?
exercises.explanation: The dua covers both known and unknown shirk - a daily reminder that motives can hide even from the one doing the deed.

source.text: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowingly associating anything with You, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know.

options.text: "Allahumma inni a’udhu bika an ushrika bika wa ana a’lam, wa astaghfiruka lima la a’lam"

exercises.prompt: Your daily Quran reading is now recorded and posted for an audience. How can riya creep in?

source.text: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends to be seen by people.

options.text: The practice turns into content for people instead of worship for Allah
